subject: MSstatsTMT: How are values imputed when maxQuantileforCensored=NULL ?

messages.author: b4f45db4340c181c
messages.subject: MSstatsTMT: How are values imputed when maxQuantileforCensored=NULL ?
parts:
Hi MSstatsTMT team,

Please explain how missing values are imputed when the following settings are applied to the proteinSummarization method:
method="msstats", 
MBimpute=FALSE, 
maxQuantileforCensored=NULL

I've read the documentation, paper and looked at the YouTube videos, but it's still not clear to me how the values for imputation are chosen.

From the documentation:
MBimpute:
only for method="msstats". TRUE (default) imputes missing values by Accelated failure model. FALSE uses minimum value to impute the missing value for each peptide precursor ion.

maxQuantileforCensored:
We assume missing values are censored. maxQuantileforCensored is Maximum quantile for deciding censored missing value, for instance, 0.999. Default is Null.


My understanding is:
  • only NaN values will be imputed
  • I can see that for each feature a different value is imputed, but what's the basis for this imputation?

Thank you for all your efforts!!

Best,
David
